newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends higher in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends higher in dull trade.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended higher on local covering but trading continued to be dull due to year-end factors, dealers said.
"The market remained quiet with nothing much happening in the market because everyone is in the festive holiday mood," a dealer said, adding that a lack of consumer demand also dampened activity.
Dealers expect the market to be featureless for the greater part of this week with most local and foreign players staying for away for the Christmas celebration.
Tight supply, because of rains in some main growing areas, also aided prices, dealers said.
At the close, January RSS buyer Ones rose a cent to 317.50 cents ($1.26) a kg and January SMR 20 buyer was up half a cent at 308.50 cents.
The INRO five-day average was 243.14 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Dec 20 from 243.22 on Dec 19. The daily indicator was 241.62 against 243.18. -- Tan Lee Lee (603-230-7510) ($1=2.5260 ringgit)
